title: Scripture is not so dark that necessary doctrine cannot be gathered — pastors help without replacing it
source_text: XLII. Qualiscunque ergo sit Scripturae obscuritas, negamus illam ita obscuram esse, quin tota doctrina ad fidem & mores necessaria ex ea indubie & certo colligi possit ab attento & perito lectore. Nec enim asserimus Scripturam ita claram esse in omnibus quae sunt ad fidem & salutem alicujus momenti, ut ad scopum ejus assequendum, & doctrinam sacram inde eruendam, nullo sit opus labore, studio & diligentia: sed per se fidelis quisque statim & sine ullo adjumento illam satis intelligere possit. Quamvis enim Scripturae sensus saepe ita in promptu sit, ut probatione non egeat, & ingerat se vel invitis, nonnunquam tamen, ut sensus Scripturae eruatur, & splendeat, verba diligenter ponderanda sunt, praecedentia & sequentia accurate expendenda, & parallela loca conferenda, sepositis praejudiciis, & compositis animi affectibus. Qua in re opus est ut Pastores praeeant plebi curae suae commissae, tam privatis sermonibus, quam publicis concionibus, ac etiam, quum res exigit, editis scriptis diversi generis, in quibus Scripturam explicent & applicent ad varios usus populi Christiani. Ad hoc enim inter alia Deus Ecclesiae dedit Pastores & Doctores, ut Dei verbum in Scriptura contentum exponerent, Scripturae sensum aperirent, & in ejus intelligentiam plebem fidelem quasi manu ducerent.
pass_a_gloss: Of whatever kind therefore the obscurity of Scripture be, we deny that it is so obscure that the whole doctrine necessary to faith and manners cannot be gathered from it undoubtingly and certainly by an attentive and skilled reader. For we do not assert that Scripture is so clear in all things which are of any moment for faith and salvation, that for attaining its scope, and drawing sacred doctrine thence, there is need of no labor, study, and diligence: but that every believer by himself at once and without any help can sufficiently understand it. For although the sense of Scripture is often so ready to hand that it needs no proof, and thrusts itself even on the unwilling, yet sometimes, that the sense of Scripture may be drawn out and shine, the words are to be diligently weighed, the preceding and following accurately considered, and parallel places compared, prejudices laid aside, and the affections of the mind composed. In which matter there is need that Pastors go before the people committed to their care, both by private discourses and by public sermons, and also, when the matter requires, by published writings of diverse kinds, in which they explain Scripture and apply it to the various uses of the Christian people. For to this among other things God gave Pastors and Doctors to the Church, that they might expound the word of God contained in Scripture, open the sense of Scripture, and as it were lead the faithful people by the hand into its understanding.
pass_b_english: Whatever Scripture's obscurity, necessary faith-and-life doctrine can still be gathered certainly by an attentive, skilled reader.
Clarity is not instant ease without labor — weighing words, context, parallels, and purged affections still matter.
Pastors and teachers rightly go before the flock in private, pulpit, and writing.
God gave them to open Scripture's sense — not to replace Scripture as another divine word.
